record.statement: A start is allowed when the balance is at or above the start threshold; one credit below is refused.
examples: With a threshold of 70, a balance of 70 may start and 69 may not.

record.statement: An entry that would take a balance below MinBalanceCredits is refused with ErrBalanceOutOfRange and nothing is applied; landing exactly on the minimum is applied.
examples: An adjustment of MinBalanceCredits-1 on a fresh account is refused and the balance stays 0.

record.statement: A batch is refused before anything is saved unless it has 1 to 10 trials and 1 to 50 test cases with no test case repeated.
examples: 11 trials, 51 test cases, or the same test case twice is refused with 400.

record.statement: A batch is read by its id together with the asking Workspace, so another Workspace's batch reads as not found.
examples: A stranger asking for someone else's batch report gets 404.

record.statement: A batch is refused as a whole, naming every unconfirmed test case, when any of its test cases lacks confirmed run permissions.
examples: Two test cases, one unconfirmed: 422 naming only that one, and nothing is saved.

record.statement: A batch paused for 30 days stops with reason paused_too_long; one paused for less stays paused and can be resumed from its next unrun trial.
examples: Paused 30 days and a minute stops; 29 days 23 hours stays paused.

record.statement: When a batch's creator no longer exists, the batch stops as creator_gone instead of starting another trial with no actor.
examples: The creator's account is removed mid-batch; the next advance stops the batch and starts nothing.

record.statement: When starting a batch's next trial finds its target gone, the batch stops with reason target_gone and starts no further trial.
examples: A test case deleted mid-batch: the batch becomes stopped with target_gone.

record.statement: A package the packager has built is refused when its zip exceeds the produced-size ceiling, and the refusal is counted.
examples: A zip one byte over the ceiling is refused.

record.statement: Replaying a charge under the same idempotency key reports it as existing and leaves one cost event, one ledger entry and one debit.
examples: Charging the same creation-step key twice debits 13 credits once.

record.statement: A charge without a kind, an idempotency key or a user is refused as invalid.
examples: A charge with an empty kind returns ErrInvalid.

record.statement: A cost event without a kind or an idempotency key is refused as invalid and nothing is recorded.
examples: Recording a cost event with an empty idempotency key returns ErrInvalid.

record.statement: Raising a creation budget is refused unless the new amount is finite, strictly above the current budget and within the ceiling.
examples: Raising 0.5 to 0.5 is refused.

record.statement: A creation command is refused as a conflict unless its expected revision equals the stored one.
examples: A command for revision 2 against revision 3 conflicts.

record.statement: Selecting the same reference Skill twice is refused.
examples: Selecting one skill twice is refused as invalid.

record.statement: Selecting more than three reference Skills is refused.
examples: Selecting four references is refused as invalid.

record.statement: Creation limits are usable only when the retention outlasts the session timeout plus the longest step that can start just before it: the call timeout, ten seconds of slack and sixty seconds to revoke the key, search ahead and settle; otherwise a session row could be deleted before its last step's spend is charged.
examples: With a one-minute session and a one-second call timeout, a retention of one minute and seventy-one seconds is usable and one second less is not.

record.statement: A creation may take a step only while it has taken fewer than its approved number of steps, even with budget left.
examples: With budget left, the last approved step is allowed and none after it.

record.statement: Suggesting acceptance criteria is a model call the user starts, so it is open only to invited accounts, refused before the model is called when the test case already holds the most criteria it may or when the owner's credit balance is below the start threshold for suggest_criteria, and debited by the usage the gateway reported once the model answers; it never proposes more criteria than there is room for.
examples: With no suggest_criteria statistics the threshold is the 70-credit fallback: a balance of 69 is refused with no model call and nothing charged; a balance of 70 is allowed and a $0.01 answer debits 13 credits at the default markup.
With 19 of 20 criteria a suggestion answers with one proposal out of three; with 20 it answers 413 and the model is not called.

record.statement: A deletion sweep purges a Skill and its versions only once the Skill's deletion is older than the grace period; a sweep given a non-positive grace is refused and purges nothing.
examples: A Skill deleted a moment ago survives a 30-day sweep and a sweep with zero grace is refused; one deleted 31 days ago with nothing depending on it is purged.

record.statement: When a published Skill is deleted its publication retires; for 90 days after that its old address still answers withdrawn and the publisher cannot give its name to another Skill; after 90 days the name passes to another of the same publisher's Skills and the address follows it.
examples: Reusing the name 89 days 23 hours after the delete answers 409 name_held; 90 days and a minute after, it publishes and the old address serves the successor.

record.statement: A development login name longer than 64 characters is refused with 400 before any account is touched.
examples: A 64-character name logs in; 65 characters answer 400.

record.statement: A download artifact is read by its id together with the asking Workspace, so another Workspace's artifact can be neither seen nor fetched.
examples: A stranger asking for someone else's download gets 404.

record.statement: A feedback request body over 8 KiB is refused before any field is read.
examples: A body padded past 8 KiB answers 400 and stores nothing.

record.statement: A reported build id is kept only when it is non-blank and at most 64 bytes; otherwise it is dropped and the report is still accepted.
examples: A 65-character build id is stored as absent; a 64-character one is kept.

record.statement: A feedback kind must be blocking_issue or need_signal; any other or a missing kind is refused with 400.
examples: kind praise answers 400.

record.statement: A feedback message is trimmed, must be non-blank and may hold at most 2000 characters; otherwise it is refused with 400.
examples: A 2001-character message answers 400; exactly 2000 is accepted.

record.statement: Confirming or declining a fetch is refused unless a fetch permission question is pending.
examples: confirm_fetch when nobody asked is an invalid command.

record.statement: An import from a URL accepts a package of exactly the zip ceiling and refuses one byte more.
examples: A server answering with one byte over the ceiling is refused naming the 10.0 MB limit.

record.statement: A fork starts with its source's access restriction, so forking cannot get around a licensing hold.
examples: Forking a skill held for licence review gives a held fork whose files answer 403.

record.statement: A fork of a fork reuses the base name instead of growing it, treating only an ordinal of two or more as a series number.
examples: Forking tidy-csv-fork-2 proposes tidy-csv-fork, while tidy-csv-fork-1 is a plain name.

record.statement: A version of uploaded content cannot be added to a generated skill; it is refused as a name collision and consumes no version number.
examples: Uploading a package named like a generated skill is refused.

record.statement: A generated skill's redistribution can be neither blocked nor allowed; it stays generated.
examples: Blocking a generated skill is refused as generated_is_permanent.

record.statement: A generation's task description counts characters, not bytes: one shorter than 8 characters without a diagram is refused as blank, one longer than 4000 is refused as too long, and both bounds themselves are accepted; with no description, a diagram is required.
examples: Eight letters are accepted, seven are refused as blank; 4000 CJK characters are accepted, 4001 are refused.

record.statement: A diagram attached to a generation must be a non-empty image of an allowed type and at most 4,000,000 bytes; a diagram of exactly that size is accepted.
examples: A 4,000,000-byte PNG is accepted; one byte more is refused before the gateway.

record.statement: A generation names at most three reference skills; three are accepted and four are refused before the gateway.
examples: Three references reach the gateway; four are refused.

record.statement: An idempotency key already used for an operator entry is refused with ErrGrantKeyReused when it is presented with another kind or another amount, and the balance is unchanged.
examples: Key k granted 50; k presented again for 60 or as a topup is refused and the balance stays 50.

record.statement: An operator entry is refused when its credits are zero, its trimmed reason is empty, or its user, operator or idempotency key is missing; its kind must be grant, topup or adjustment.
examples: A 50-credit grant whose reason is only spaces is refused.

record.statement: A purge keeps the row of a skill that has test cases or a version referenced by a run, a download or a bundle; the deleted-skill sweep also keeps a skill while its publication is unretired or retired less than the ninety-day name hold ago, and while an operator takedown or access restriction is in force on it. An operator can take down or restrict a skill its owner has deleted until the sweep purges it, and the operator's skill search lists such a skill with when it was deleted.
examples: A deleted skill past grace that has test cases survives the sweep.
A deleted skill whose publication retired 89 days 23 hours ago survives the sweep; at 90 days and a minute it is purged.
A skill its owner deleted while an operator takedown was in force survives the sweep past grace; after the operator lifts the takedown the next sweep purges it.
A skill its owner deleted before any complaint is found by the operator's search, taken down or restricted, and then survives the sweep past grace; a deleted skill nobody holds is purged.

record.statement: A new version must declare the same name as its Skill; another name is refused as version_name_mismatch and neither a version nor the summary changes.
examples: Uploading a package named split-csv as a version of tidy-notes is blocked.

record.statement: A package expires exactly the configured retention after it is built.
examples: With a seven-day retention, a package built now expires in seven days.

record.statement: A package built for a recipient never selects test cases, whatever the include flag says.
examples: A recipient package asked to include test cases holds none.

record.statement: Planning a package refuses a version that belongs to another Skill, so one Skill's gates are never applied to another Skill's files.
examples: Asking for Skill A with a version of Skill B is not found.

record.statement: A person's message is refused when blank or longer than 4000 characters.
examples: 4000 characters are accepted; 4001 are refused.

record.statement: An artifact the provider reports may name only the archive object the platform derived for the attempt; any other object key is refused.
examples: A manifest entry naming another Workspace's dataset object is refused as outside its write grant.

record.statement: A Skill that already has a publication cannot be republished under another name; the request is refused as name_is_permanent and the publication keeps its name.
examples: A Skill published as foo and republished as another-name answers 409 name_is_permanent.

record.statement: Publishing a Skill with a version of another Skill is answered not found, so one Skill's gates never pass another Skill's files.
examples: Publishing Skill A with Skill B's version answers 404.

record.statement: The start check refuses an account that account facts report missing or purged, before reading any balance.
examples: CanStart for a purged user returns ErrAccountGone.

record.statement: When account facts report the user missing or purged, a grant and a charge are refused with ErrAccountGone and nothing is recorded.
examples: A charge to a purged account leaves no cost event and no debit.

record.statement: An unexpired session stops counting once its account is being purged or has been deleted.
examples: A user whose purge has started gets 401 with a still-valid cookie.

record.statement: A quote shorter than twelve characters cannot be matched to a verified excerpt as suggestion evidence.
examples: Evidence "e" inside a verified excerpt is refused.

record.statement: A provider refusal that is neither unavailable nor full is final, so no further attempt starts.
examples: A provider answering 400 leaves the run failed after exactly one attempt.

record.statement: When Run refuses a simulated person's answer because the owner's credit or run quota ran out, the batch pauses with that reason instead of closing the trial; a paused batch answers nothing, and resuming it gives the answers still owed.
examples: An answer refused for credit_balance leaves the batch paused and the trial unanswered; topping up without resuming still answers nothing; resuming answers it and the batch is launched again.

record.statement: Releasing a skill for redistribution is refused when the claimed licence differs from the one its newest version records, and the stored value is unchanged.
examples: A release claiming Apache-2.0 for a version that records MIT is refused as license_mismatch.

record.statement: Starting a session with an id already used returns that session only for the same message and budget; a different request with the same id is refused as a replay mismatch.
examples: The same id with another message is refused.

record.statement: Replaying a grant under the same key returns the current balance and writes no second audit event.
examples: Granting twice with the same key returns 50 both times and writes one audit event.

record.statement: Restricting a skill with a reason code outside the known set is refused, listing the known codes.
examples: The reason 'invented' is refused as an unknown reason code.

record.statement: A rubric is accepted only when every item names an existing acceptance criterion, and deleting a criterion removes its rubric item.
examples: A rubric item naming not-a-criterion answers 400.

record.statement: A Run and its evaluation appear as one item; when the evaluation is more urgent, or equally urgent and newer, its classification and status replace the Run's, and the item's time is the later of the two.
examples: A succeeded Run at 08:00 whose evaluation is not_met at 09:00 shows as needs attention at 09:00.

record.statement: The search limit must be a whole number from 1 to 100; anything else is refused.
examples: limit=100 is accepted and limit=101 answers 400.

record.statement: A page the activity service serves says it is complete and names all contracted sources, even when it holds no items.
examples: An empty workspace gets complete=true with the five sources listed.

record.statement: A session is refused before any database work when its budget is below one model call's cost or above the session ceiling.
examples: A budget just over the ceiling is refused as out of band.

record.statement: A session counts only strictly before its expiry; at the expiry instant it is already signed out.
examples: A session expiring exactly now is invalid.

record.statement: The Workspace carried by a signed-in request is reused only when asking about its own owner; any other account's Workspace is read from its owner.
examples: Inside Alice's request, asking for Bob's Workspace returns Bob's, not Alice's.

record.statement: Deleting a download removes its stored object only when no other live artifact shares it.
examples: Deleting one of two live artifacts sharing an object keeps the object.

record.statement: A batch answers a trial's questions as the simulated person only when the trial's conversation ended successfully, its test case has facts and the creator still exists; otherwise the questions are left for a real person.
examples: A succeeded run whose test case has no facts gets no simulated reply.

record.statement: A Skill already taken down cannot be taken down again, except that an operator's takedown supersedes the owner's own: the Skill stays down, now as the operator's, and only an operator lifts it. Any other second attempt is refused and the Skill stays down.
examples: A second report against a taken-down Skill is refused as already_taken_down.
An operator taking down a Skill its owner already took down succeeds; the owner can no longer restore it.

record.statement: The Skill listing accepts a limit of 1 to 100 and a non-negative offset; any other value, including an empty or non-integer one, is refused.
examples: limit=101 is refused.

record.statement: A package is refused when SKILL.md points at a file or directory the packager leaves out, since the download would miss what its own instructions use.
examples: SKILL.md linking node_modules/helper.js blocks the package as file_removed_by_packager.

record.statement: A snapshot's content hash covers the prompt with the criteria, datasets, rubric and facts, so any edit freezes a new snapshot and earlier ones stay as they were.
examples: Snapshotting after changing the prompt gives a different hash and leaves the first snapshot's prompt unchanged.

record.statement: A version is written only when its source carries the provenance its kind requires: git needs a URL and no generator fields, an upload has neither, a generated source needs a model and prompt version and no URL; anything else is refused with ErrIncompleteProvenance.
examples: An upload claiming a URL is refused with ErrIncompleteProvenance.

record.statement: A purge keeps a source skill while any fork of it stays, transitively down fork chains.
examples: A deleted skill forked by another user's live skill survives the sweep.

record.statement: Recording a cost event ignores the caller's cancellation and runs under its own deadline, so a client disconnect cannot lose a cost event.
examples: Recording with an already-cancelled request still stores the event.

record.statement: A Workspace that has used its daily allowance in the trailing 24 hours is refused with reason quota_daily, and the message says when it resets.
examples: A Workspace with 5 runs in the last 24 hours is refused a sixth.

record.statement: A Workspace that has used its rolling-window allowance is refused with reason quota_window, and the message says when the next one frees up.
examples: A Workspace with 30 runs in the last 30 days but none today is refused.

record.statement: A credit statement returns at most one page of entries and says whether more remain, by asking for one entry past the page.
examples: With 51 entries a statement returns 50 and says more remain; with 50 it says none remain.

record.statement: A paid step may proceed only when the balance minus the credits billed for its reservation stays at or above the configured debt floor.
examples: With a floor of -50 and 13 credits reserved, a balance of -37 may continue and -38 may not.

record.statement: A stored source that now fails import validation is not packaged, except for errors inside a directory the packager leaves out anyway.
examples: A SKILL.md without front matter blocks the package as validation_blocked.

record.statement: A takedown with an empty or whitespace-only reason is refused and the Skill stays up.
examples: A takedown with reason ' \t\n' is refused as takedown_reason_missing.

record.statement: Forking a taken-down skill finds nothing.
examples: Forking a catalogue skill an operator took down answers not found.

record.statement: A Skill an operator took down cannot be published; the request is answered not found and no publication is created.
examples: Publishing a taken-down Skill answers 404 and leaves no publication.

record.statement: A taken-down Skill refuses every new version as skill_taken_down and gains no version row; in a re-import of several Skills the others still import.
examples: After a takedown, uploading tidy-notes again is blocked and it keeps one version.

record.statement: The test case list takes a limit from 1 to 101 inclusive and defaults to 51, one row more than a page shows so the client can tell whether another page exists; 0, 102, a non-integer and an empty limit are refused, never replaced by the default.
examples: limit=101 lists; limit=102 and limit= answer 400; no limit lists 51.

record.statement: The test case list takes an offset from 0 to 2147483647 as a plain decimal integer; a negative, fractional, hexadecimal, empty or larger value is refused rather than read as 0.
examples: offset=2147483647 lists; offset=2147483648, offset=0x10 and offset=-1 answer 400.

record.statement: A test case is marked prompt-varied only when its trials started from more than one distinct prompt.
examples: Trials started from two different prompt hashes are marked varied.

record.statement: When a Run reaches its deadline while an attempt is still live, the attempt is finished as timed out in the same step that moves the Run to timed_out, whether the deadline is noticed by the Run's own job or by the supervisor; a timed-out Run never leaves a live attempt behind.
examples: A sandbox still running at the deadline: the Run becomes timed_out and its attempt carries the timeout error class.
A Run whose job died before its deadline: the supervisor times it out and closes the attempt the job left live.

record.statement: An event's attempt must be from 1 to 100000; a larger attempt is refused.
examples: An event with attempt 100001 is refused as invalid.

record.statement: A trace cursor that is negative or not a number answers 400 in every view.
examples: after=-1 answers 400.

record.statement: An event's time must fall between a few minutes in the future and the token's lifetime in the past; epoch or far-future timestamps are refused.
examples: An event timestamped four years ahead is refused.

record.statement: One trace ingestion request carries at most 1000 events; a larger batch is refused with 413 before any event is judged.
examples: 1000 events reach ingestion; 1001 events answer 413 too many events in one batch.

record.statement: A trace event whose payload exceeds 96 KiB is refused as invalid; exactly 96 KiB is accepted.
examples: A payload of 98305 bytes is refused.

record.statement: An event whose emitted_by is not a known producer is refused.
examples: An event emitted by 'browser' is refused as invalid.

record.statement: An event is accepted only under a 1.x schema version; another major version is refused while additive minor versions are accepted.
examples: schema_version 2.0 is refused; 1.7 is accepted.

record.statement: An event's seq must be from 1 to 100000; a larger seq is refused.
examples: An event with seq 100001 is refused as invalid.

record.statement: An event whose status is not one of the known outcomes is refused.
examples: An event with status 'exploded' is refused as invalid.

record.statement: A simulated answer refused because the conversation has no further round closes the trial instead of failing the batch.
examples: A batch settles once no trial runs and no simulated answer is owed.

record.statement: Search fetches one row past the limit; when more than the limit match, it returns the limit, marks the page truncated and reports the full total.
examples: limit=1 over five matching skills returns one result, truncated, with total 5.

record.statement: Publishing scans the version's stored package and refuses as validation_blocked when it finds any validation error; no publication is recorded.
examples: A version carrying a credential in .env answers 422 validation_blocked and leaves no publication row.

record.statement: A workspace holds at most one generation at a time across every API instance: a second request while a lease is live is refused as in flight, another workspace is unaffected, and an expired lease can be taken over.
examples: Two API instances asking for the same workspace: the first holds the slot and the second is refused; a different workspace still generates.

record.statement: Before any package object is stored, a Workspace that may not store objects is answered not found and nothing is written.
examples: A Workspace whose lifecycle forbids storage gets 404 and no object.

record.statement: Until a Workspace's first window ends, its window ceiling is the first-window allowance, and its window resets at the earlier of that end and the rolling reset; from the moment the first window ends the ordinary window ceiling applies.
examples: One second before its first 30 days end a Workspace's ceiling is 20; at the moment they end it is 30.

record.statement: Purging a deleted account runs the purge step of every Context that keeps data for its workspace (analytics, testlab, run, packaging, creation, eval, publishing, registry, ingest) together with the object listings of testlab, run and packaging; when any of them is missing, the purge refuses to start instead of purging part of the account.
examples: An account past its grace period has its graders, creation sessions, publications and skills removed in one purge.
A deployment wired without the eval purge step refuses every account purge and names eval as missing.
Registry's step runs before ingest's, so import sources no remaining version points at are removed in the same purge.

record.statement: Every owner source of the feed is read with the requesting Workspace's id, so no Workspace sees another's activity.
examples: Alice's Workspace lists her four items; Bob's lists none.

record.statement: Adopting a reference names exactly one listed Skill.
examples: Adopting two skills at once is refused.

record.statement: A run of a skill under an access restriction is refused when it is created, and a run that was queued before the restriction was set fails as policy_refused at dispatch, before any sandbox receives the package; while the restriction cannot be read the run stays queued.
examples: A run queued before an operator sets license-review fails as policy_refused naming the license review, and the sandbox sees no dispatch; after the restriction is cleared a new run succeeds.

record.statement: An access restriction must carry a non-blank reason code; a blank one is refused and the Skill's restriction is unchanged. A restriction is lifted with none, not blank.
examples: Setting the restriction to '  ' is refused and the column stays empty.

record.statement: Purging an account detaches its funnel events from the Workspace and user, and erases its feedback reports' text, page and Run link, keeping only each report's kind and time for counting.
examples: After the purge a report that said 'I wanted a python profile' on /runs/x keeps its kind need_signal and its time, with no message, page, Run, Workspace or user.

record.statement: A cursor the feed did not issue is refused as invalid before any owner source is read.
examples: cursor=not-a-cursor is refused and no reader is called.

record.statement: A cursor without a kind or without a source id is refused as invalid.
examples: A cursor with an empty source_id is refused.

record.statement: A cursor naming a priority rank outside 0 to 3 is refused as invalid, so a forged cursor cannot reach a rank the feed does not have.
examples: A cursor with rank 4 is refused; rank 3 is accepted.

record.statement: The activity feed refuses a page limit outside 1 to 100 with 400.
examples: limit=0 and limit=101 both answer 400.

record.statement: An allowance is enforced only when it has a window length and at least one ceiling; a zero or partial configuration refuses nothing.
examples: Daily 5, window 30 but no window length is not enforced.

record.statement: An approval is refused as stale and records nothing unless it names the search snapshot digest the reviewer saw; a revocation needs no such proof.
examples: Text re-enriched while the reviewer reads makes an approval with the old digest fail with 409 and no review row.

record.statement: When embeddings are missing or fail, search returns the lexical results and says it is degraded, rather than failing the request.
examples: With the embedding endpoint returning 502, a lexically matching skill is still returned with degraded set and a reason.

record.statement: A saved or cancelled creation accepts no command, not even cancel.
examples: Cancelling a saved creation is refused as invalid.

record.statement: A package is not served once it has expired, been purged or is not scan-available.
examples: Fetching an expired download answers gone.

record.statement: An exposure review is refused as stale unless it names the current release and the review sequence its reviewer saw.
examples: Two reviewers open sequence 0; after one approves, the other's revocation at sequence 0 is refused as stale.

record.statement: An exposure review is refused before any lookup unless its decision is approved or revoked and it carries a non-blank reason.
examples: An approval whose reason is only spaces answers 422 reason_missing.

record.statement: Saving an improved version is refused with ErrBaseVersionMoved when the Skill's newest version is no longer the version the improvement was made to; content identical to an existing version is deduplicated first.
examples: Suggestions applied to v1 after v2 was saved are refused as target_changed.

record.statement: An event sent under a sandbox ingestion token is refused unless the sandbox emitted it; orchestrator and llm_service events cannot arrive that way.
examples: An orchestrator event sent with the sandbox token is counted as rejected and not stored.

record.statement: A GitHub login callback is refused with 401 before any code exchange unless its state matches the state cookie set when the login began.
examples: A callback with state abc and a state cookie of other answers 401.

record.statement: An operator's note on an agent change is at most the contract's cap counted in characters; one more is refused with 400.
examples: A note of exactly the cap in Chinese characters is accepted; one more is refused.

record.statement: An operator note longer than the contract's cap is refused; a note of exactly the cap is accepted.
examples: A takedown note one character over the cap answers 400.

record.statement: The operator note cap counts characters, not bytes, so a note of Chinese characters up to the cap is accepted.
examples: A note of exactly the cap in Chinese characters is accepted; one more is refused.

record.statement: A caller's origin key returns the run it already started for the same Skill Version and is refused for a different version.
examples: The same key on another version is refused; on the same version it returns the same run.

record.statement: A trace ingestion body over 4 MiB answers 413 as too large, apart from a body that fails while being read, which answers 400.
examples: A body of 4 MiB and one byte answers 413.

record.statement: The owner may undo a takedown the owner made, within 30 days of it; a takedown an operator made, or one whose origin is unknown, only an operator lifts, at any time; restoring a Skill that is not taken down is refused.
examples: An owner's takedown exactly 30 days old is restored; 30 days and a second is refused; an operator's takedown an hour old is refused to the owner and lifted by an operator.

record.statement: A run no provider has accepted waits for a slot up to the slot-wait limit plus the time dispatch was paused for it, and is timed out with a queue reason just past that.
examples: A run with no provider handle is still waiting at creation plus the limit, and expired a moment later.

record.statement: When any activity source cannot be read, the request answers 503 with complete=false, the failed sources and no items.
examples: A failing run reader gives 503 naming runs.

record.statement: An item whose classification the feed does not know ranks below needs-attention, in-progress and recent items.
examples: An item classified 'something-new' sorts after a recent one, even when newer.

record.statement: Each reported artifact must be no larger than the run's frozen per-file limit, and their total within its frozen total limit, before anything is persisted.
examples: A file one byte over the per-file limit is refused.

record.statement: At most ten suggestions are stored for one evaluation; the rest are counted as dropped over the cap.
examples: Twelve citable proposals store ten.

record.statement: A stored package is served only while the Skill is still releasable: a taken-down, held or non-redistributable Skill makes its already built packages unavailable for download and shows them as withheld in the list.
examples: A package built yesterday, then the Skill is taken down: the content route answers not found and the list shows serve_state withheld.
A plugin package is withheld if any of its member Skill Versions is held, taken down or not redistributable.

record.statement: An evaluation batch waits when Run refuses a trial with a refusal Run says will pass on its own, including a run quota that could not be counted; pauses with the reason recorded when the refusal is one the owner can outwait or fix, a credit top-up or a used-up daily or windowed run quota; and stops with the reason recorded on any other refusal.
examples: A credit_balance refusal pauses the batch with only its first trial run; a missing permission confirmation stops it.
A quota_daily or quota_window refusal pauses the batch; a quota_unavailable refusal makes it wait.

record.statement: Two batches are compared only on test cases judged in both; a test case judged in only one counts as unpaired, not as better, worse or tied.
examples: A test case judged in the candidate but not the reference adds to unpaired.

record.statement: While a P1 incident halt covers the pool or an attempt's provider, cleanup leaves that attempt's sandbox standing and does not mark the Run cleaned, so the scene stays preserved until an operator lifts the halt.
examples: A pool-wide incident halt holds every finished Run's sandbox.
A halt naming one provider holds only the sandboxes on that provider.
A capacity pause, which is not an incident, does not hold cleanup.

record.statement: Once an Account has started purging or is deleted, deletion can neither be requested nor cancelled; the user is told it is irreversible (HTTP 409).
examples: Cancelling a deletion whose purge has started answers 409 'deletion is already irreversible'.
Requesting deletion for an already deleted Account answers 409.

record.statement: Delisting writes an audit event only when it changes the publication, so delisting twice records one delist.
examples: Delisting an already delisted publication adds no second audit event.

record.statement: The development login route exists only when development login is enabled; otherwise it answers 404.
examples: With development login off, POST /auth/dev/login answers 404.

record.statement: Every dispatch to a provider carries the platform's own attempt id as its idempotency key, so a re-sent dispatch is deduplicated per attempt and no provider id stands in for the platform's identity.
examples: A run retried after a 503 dispatches its second attempt keyed by that attempt's id, not the run id.

record.statement: Changing the text of an acceptance criterion clears its confirmation, so a person must confirm the new wording.
examples: A confirmed criterion edited to add a unit comes back unconfirmed.

record.statement: evaluation_started and evaluation_completed events are refused unless the orchestrator emitted them, even from an otherwise known producer.
examples: An evaluation_completed event emitted by the sandbox is refused as invalid.

record.statement: Enabling or disabling an agent, changing its spend cap or its brake is refused with 400 when the note is blank.
examples: A whitespace-only note answers 400 and the agent stays disabled.

record.statement: A run named on a feedback report is kept only when it belongs to the reporter's Workspace; another Workspace's run is dropped and the report is still accepted.
examples: Alice reports with Bob's run id: the report is filed with no run.

record.statement: A reported page path is kept only when it starts with '/', carries no query or fragment and is at most 512 bytes; otherwise it is dropped and the report is still accepted.
examples: /skills?q=secret is stored as no page path.

record.statement: A feedback report that names a run is refused with a server error when the run ownership reader is not wired, and nothing is stored.
examples: Without the reader, a report naming a valid run id answers 500 and stores no row.

record.statement: Purging feedback removes only reports created before the retention window, and the preview counts exactly what the purge removes.
examples: With a 90-day window, reports aged 100 and 91 days are removed and a fresh one stays.

record.statement: A name held by a generated Skill takes no uploaded version, and a generated candidate takes no name held by an uploaded Skill; either way the save is refused with ErrGeneratedNameCollision.
examples: Generate pdf-extract, then upload a package named pdf-extract: refused.

record.statement: Saving content whose hash a version of the same Skill already holds returns that version as a duplicate and writes no new version.
examples: Restoring the text of an earlier version returns that version's id, marked duplicate.

record.statement: Informational findings are left out of the suggestion digest, so a disclosure cannot be quoted as proof of a problem.
examples: An info finding's excerpt is not in the digest.

record.statement: No funnel event is collected and no analytics cookie is set unless a retention period of at least one second is configured.
examples: A deployment with no retention period records no search or detail event.

record.statement: Two live accounts never share an email: emails are compared after trimming and lower-casing, a sign-up whose email belongs to a live account is refused, and an email held only by a deleted account can be used again.
examples: Signing up as ' Alice@Example.COM ' while alice@example.com belongs to a live account is refused as email-taken (HTTP 409).
Signing up with the email of an account that is already deleted succeeds and yields a session.

record.statement: Curating a skill is refused when it is not in a catalogue Workspace, and its tier is unchanged.
examples: Curating a skill imported into a user's own Workspace is refused.

record.statement: A listing records a curated version only when the Skill's tier is curated; any other tier writes none.
examples: Indexed-tier facts that carry a curated version id write none.

record.statement: Only skill, runtime, tool and dataset suggestions are stored; MCP and unknown categories are dropped.
examples: A proposal in category mcp is not stored.

record.statement: An operator entry with negative credits is refused with ErrGrantLowersBalance unless it is an adjustment.
examples: A grant of -10 is refused; the same -10 as an adjustment is applied.

record.statement: A search document is listable only once its enrichment is finished or it has an embedding a vector search can find. An enrichment whose embedding call failed is still stored as enriched, without a vector, so it is listable at once; the enrichment backfill later embeds that stored text without calling the enrichment model again, and stores the vector only if the document has not been rewritten since it was claimed.
examples: A pending document without a vector is not listable; the same document with a vector is.

The enrichment answers and the embedding call fails: the document is enriched and listable without a vector; the next backfill pass makes one embedding call and no enrichment call, and a vector computed before a re-import rewrote the document is dropped.

record.statement: Only a Skill whose redistribution verdict is allowed, self_supplied or generated may be packaged; blocked gives not_redistributable and every other value, including an empty one, is treated as license_unknown.
examples: redistribution = allowed, self_supplied or generated: the build proceeds.
redistribution = blocked: refused as not_redistributable.
redistribution = '' or an unrecognised string: refused as license_unknown, unconfirmed license counts as not allowed.

record.statement: Recomputing statistics sweeps idle session summaries first only for the creation session statistic and only when an idle window is configured.
examples: Recomputing the creation step statistic sweeps no sessions.

record.statement: An operator route lets a request through only for a user on the operator roster; anyone else gets 404 and a refused signed-in user is audited.
examples: A signed-in non-operator asking for /admin/dispatch gets 404 and one operator-refused audit row.

record.statement: After a creation session's deadline only cancel and the three save commands (materialize, finalize, confirm duplicate), none of which calls the model, are accepted; every other command is refused.
examples: A draft-ready session past its deadline saves; a message or a budget raise is refused.

record.statement: A publication is offered only while it is published and its Skill exists, is not taken down, is not held and still passes the release gate; otherwise the first failing reason, in the order delisted, withdrawn, taken_down, held, not_redistributable, is reported.
examples: A delisted publication whose Skill is also taken down reports delisted.

record.statement: An account's stored files are removed before its database rows are erased, and the rows are erased in one transaction, so a failure leaves rows pointing at missing files that the next sweep can finish, never a file that no row names.
examples: If the object store fails mid-purge, the account stays claimed and the next sweep retries the deletion.

record.statement: An account purge starts only when the deletion request is older than the 30-day grace at the moment of claiming and every Run in each of the Account's workspaces has finished cleanup; otherwise the purge is deferred (not failed) and retried by a later sweep.
examples: A request made now is not claimed by a sweep whose cutoff is 30 days ago; the Account does not start purging.
An Account with a Run still cleaning up its sandbox is skipped this sweep without an error.

record.statement: Raising the budget of a failed creation returns it to waiting for input; any other state is kept, and no step is queued.
examples: A failed session whose budget is raised waits for input.

record.statement: Releasing the brake when none is engaged succeeds without recording a brake-released audit event.
examples: A second release adds no brake_released event.

record.statement: A Workspace without a registered publisher name cannot release; the release is refused with ErrNoPublisher.
examples: A Workspace with no publishers row is refused as no_publisher.

record.statement: The remaining allowance a Workspace sees is clamped at zero; an overspent Workspace reads 0, not a negative number.
examples: Limit 5 with 7 used reads 0 remaining.

record.statement: Re-submitting an operator entry under the same idempotency key returns the current balance without applying it or writing a second audit entry.
examples: Two identical 50-credit grants under one key leave the balance at 50 with one audit entry.

record.statement: Publishing the published latest version again, with the same content and the same declared licence, adds no release, so its exposure review is kept; declaring a different licence for that version adds a release.
examples: Publishing v1 twice leaves exactly one release; publishing it again with MIT adds a second, and once more with MIT still leaves two.

record.statement: A Run's activity item asks for attention when it failed or timed out, is in progress from queued through evaluating, and is recent once it succeeded or was cancelled; a status the Run context does not know asks for attention.
examples: A timed-out Run shows 試跑逾時 as needs attention; a cancelled one shows 已取消 as recent.

record.statement: The raw session token exists only in the cookie handed to the user; the platform stores and looks up only its SHA-256 hash.
examples: Reading the sessions table never reveals a token that can be replayed as a cookie.

record.statement: A start threshold uses recorded cost statistics only while their window ended within the statistics shelf life; older statistics give the fixed fallback, marked estimated.
examples: Statistics whose window ended an hour past the shelf life give the fallback threshold, estimated.

record.statement: A Skill that the platform has taken down, or whose content is held for an unresolved license question, cannot be built into a package; the refusal names taken_down or license_hold.
examples: A taken-down Skill: building any version answers blocked_reason taken_down.
A Skill with access_restricted set and not taken down: blocked_reason license_hold.
A Skill that is both taken down and restricted reports taken_down, because the taken-down check runs first.

record.statement: If any owner source of the feed cannot be read or is not configured, no partial page is returned; the request fails naming every source that failed.
examples: The evaluation store errors and the publishing reader is missing: the error names both and no items are returned.

record.statement: The feed is ordered by priority, then newest first, then kind, then source id, and a cursor resumes strictly after the last item returned, so pages neither repeat nor skip an item.
examples: Items c (needs attention), a and b (recent, same time) with limit 2 page as [c, a] then [b].

record.statement: The activity service itself refuses a page limit below 1 or above 100, whatever its caller checked.
examples: A limit of 101 is refused; 100 is served.

record.statement: The catalogue workspace never generates skills; a generation request in it is refused before anything else is checked.
examples: A generation asked of the catalogue workspace is refused as not for the catalogue.

record.statement: By default a Workspace may start 5 runs a day and 30 per 30 days, and 20 in its first 30 days.
examples: An unconfigured deployment refuses a sixth run in one day.

record.statement: Once a provider has accepted an attempt, the run's deadline is its first dispatch plus the frozen policy's hard wall clock, not its creation time.
examples: Dispatches at 13:00 and 14:00 under a 120-second policy give a 13:02 deadline.

record.statement: A release is refused unless the Skill's redistribution is allowed, or self_supplied or generated with the author's rights statement; a license hold, a blocked licence and an unconfirmed licence are refused whatever the statement.
examples: Self-supplied content without the statement is refused as rights_not_attested; an unconfirmed licence is refused as license_unknown even with it.

record.statement: Passed criteria are left out of the suggestion digest, so their evidence cannot be cited for an improvement.
examples: A passed criterion's excerpt is not in the digest.

record.statement: A run waiting for a sandbox slot times out only after the slot-wait limit plus every stretch during which dispatch was paused for every provider that could take it; if the halt history cannot be read the run keeps waiting.
examples: A run queued forty minutes ago, fifteen of them under a pool halt, is still queued; a pool halt declared before the run queued and still held stops its clock entirely.

record.statement: Transient provider refusals start at most the configured number of attempts, after which the run fails as a provider error.
examples: With two attempts allowed and the provider answering 503 every time, the run ends failed with two attempts.

record.statement: A charge whose actual cost is unknown is recorded as an estimated cost event and debits no credits; the reserved ceiling is never billed as the cost.
examples: An unpriced call leaves the balance unchanged and records an estimated cost event.

record.statement: While a P1 incident halts dispatch, generating a skill, a creation step, a criteria suggestion and the enrichment of an imported version are refused before the model is called and nothing is charged; a creation step that was refused is not counted and the session waits for the person to send again, and an import still completes with its enrichment left pending for the backfill, which picks nothing up until the halt is lifted. An unreadable halt state counts as halted.
examples: Under a P1 halt a criteria suggestion answers 503 naming the halt, generation returns ErrModelCallsHalted, and the model stub is never called.
An import under a P1 halt is stored with its enrichment pending and the model stub never called; the backfill run under the halt enriches nothing and the version stays pending.

record.statement: While a creation is queued for or working with the model, only cancel and stop-step are accepted; other commands conflict.
examples: Answering a question while the model works conflicts.

record.statement: Withdrawing curation is allowed for any skill, inside a catalogue or not, and clears the curated version.
examples: A curated skill that left the catalogue is withdrawn and its curated version cleared.

record.compatibility_policy: The run list shows each run's current evaluation verdict as eval serves it; run does not interpret it.
Run starts and continues trials for an evaluation batch through the ports the composition root fills; Run publishes whether a refusal passes on its own and never hands its transaction to the batch.

idempotency.on_replay: returns the Run already started under that key, without admitting or charging again
idempotency.on_conflict: refused when the key already started a Run of a different Skill Version
